header:
# Town of Charlotte municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 5; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: Town of Charlotte, Selectboard meeting minutes, March 9, 2026: 'Lee Krohn welcomed Troy Krahl as a new member of the Selectboard, elected for a three-year term'; the organizational votes elected Natalie Kanner Chair and Frank Tenney Vice Chair. The board is Kanner, Tenney, Krahl, Krohn, and J.D. Herlihy. The Selectboard directory's Charlotte entry was cut off at a page turn in extraction, but it lists Troy Krahl with a three-year term, agreeing. (The signature block of the town's August 2026 Committee Handbook still names the pre-election board with Krohn as Chair; it reproduces the 2024-2025 signature page verbatim and is a template carryover, not the current roster.)

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, & County Clerks' (January 2026): lists Mary Mead as Town Clerk of Charlotte and as Town Treasurer of Charlotte.

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, & County Clerks' (January 2026): lists Mary Mead as Town Clerk of Charlotte and as Town Treasurer of Charlotte.
Town of Charlotte, 2022 Annual Town Report, Elected Town Officers table: Delinquent Tax Collector: Mary A. Mead (one-year term).

The Charlotte News, April 16, 2026, reporting a Selectboard meeting: Mead reported on the town's delinquent taxes in her capacity as collector. The News' March 2026 town-meeting results report her re-elected Delinquent Tax Collector; the town publishes no results document of its own that could be found, and the newspaper reporting is uncontradicted.
Town of Charlotte, 2022 Annual Town Report, Elected Town Officers table: Moderator (Town): Charlie Russell (one-year term).

The Charlotte News' March 2026 town-meeting results report Charlie Russell re-elected Moderator; Russell was also styled the town moderator in the News' January 2026 reporting. The town publishes no results document of its own that could be found.
Town of Charlotte, 2022 Annual Town Report, Elected Town Officers table: the town's posted election results list 'Road Commissioner (1 Year): Hugh Lewis Jr.'
The Charlotte News' March 2026 town-meeting results report Hugh Lewis Jr. re-elected Road Commissioner. The town publishes no results document of its own that could be found.

The Charlotte News, April 16, 2026: 'Patrice Machavern will continue as a town auditor until an election in March 2027,' appointed by the Selectboard to a vacancy after the March 2026 auditor contest drew no elected winner. The town's Board of Auditors is a live elected body (the town posted notice of its January 22, 2026 annual meeting). The holders of the board's other two seats are not published in any current source read.
Town of Charlotte, 2022 Annual Town Report, Elected Town Officers table: Charlotte Library Trustees serve five-year staggered terms (the table lists one term expiring each year).

The Charlotte News' March 2026 town-meeting results report Cecelia Wu elected Library Trustee to a five-year term. Janice Heilmann's term, per the town report table, expires in 2027, so she remains seated; the holders of the board's remaining seats are not published in any current source read.
Town of Charlotte, 2022 Annual Town Report, Elected Town Officers table: Cemetery Commissioners serve three-year staggered terms.
The Charlotte News' March 2026 results report the Cemetery Commissioner three-year contest as 'Write-in vacant.' Structure only: no current holder is verifiably published.

The Charlotte News' March 2026 results report the Trustee of Public Funds three-year contest as 'Write-in vacant'; the town's report table shows the board's three staggered seats. Structure only: no current holder is verifiably published.

17 V.S.A. section 2646 (official text, Vermont General Assembly) provides for the election of a grand juror at annual town meeting. Structure only: no official source publishes the current holder; the seat is left unfilled rather than guessed.

17 V.S.A. section 2646 (official text, Vermont General Assembly) provides for the election of a town agent at annual town meeting. Structure only: no official source publishes the current holder; the seat is left unfilled rather than guessed.

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists twelve Charlotte justices of the peace: Jill Abilock, Greg Cluff, Lorna Jimerson, Chea Waters Evans, Michael Krasnow, Elizabeth Langfeldt, Robin Reid, Heather Roberts, Peggy Sharpe, Carrie Spear, Mike Yantachka, and Seth Zimmerman. Chea Waters Evans is the sitting State Representative for the Chittenden-5 district (Charlotte); her existing person record is reused.

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists twelve Charlotte justices of the peace for the 2025-2026 term; they are the winners of the November 5, 2024 election for the office. The listing publishes no vote totals and no party designations for justices of the peace.
